cases.purpose: A tier S bug yields a short, grounded spec whose AC-1 is a failing reproduction, with no team run and no invented paths.
cases.pilot: The pilot has the planted bug of triage-01: the task list sorts the Due column as text, with the comparator in one UI module that has an existing test file.

inline.title: Task list sorts by due date as text, so 10 Nov comes before 2 Nov
inline.body: On the task list, click the Due column header. The rows sort as strings instead of dates. Expected: ascending by date. Only the list view is affected; the API returns ISO dates.

tierReasons.evidence: The sort comparator lives in one UI module.

security.reason: No auth or input parsing change.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json
status == "ready-for-review" && tier.confirmed == "S" && team is empty
line 3 of spec.md == "Tier: S - Builder: Sol 6.2 - Code reviewer: Opus 5.5"
spec.md has the level 2 headings Problem, Non-goals, Acceptance criteria, Design choices, Reused files, Implementation plan, Risks, Open questions, once each, in that order
every '### AC-n' block has Tag, Fixture, Action, and Expected lines, ids are AC-1..AC-k without gaps, and the ids and tags equal spec-lead.json acceptanceCriteria
AC-1 has Tag: test
every backticked path under Reused files exists in the pilot repository at baseSha
none of team-brief.md, architecture.md, infra.md, frontend.md, threat-model.md exists in the task folder
spec.md contains no U+2013 or U+2014 character
Is AC-1 a reproduction of the reported bug whose Expected line states both the correct order and how it fails on the unfixed code?
Is every Expected line something a test or a page capture could observe, with no criterion such as 'sorting works correctly'?
Do the non-goals and plan keep the change inside the list's sort logic, without API, storage, or new-feature work?

cases.purpose: Triage under-tiered a schema change. The lead must promote to L in the same run, run the team in order, and merge its decision files.
cases.pilot: The pilot of triage-02: tasks are persisted with no priority column, and the UI and API are separate modules. The pilot has a user interface and a database.

inline.title: Quick one: let tasks have a priority
inline.body: Tiny change. Add a priority (low, normal, high) to tasks, show it as a badge in the list, and let me filter by it. Should be a five minute job, just one field.

tierReasons.evidence: PLANTED: a deliberately wrong provisional tier.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json
tier.provisional == "S" && tier.confirmed == "L" && riskFlags.migration.value == true
line 3 of spec.md == "Tier: L - Builder: Opus 5.5 - Code reviewer: GPT-6.2-Astra"
team has architect with status ran, and architecture.md and team-brief.md exist in the task folder
in the run log, the architect subagent finished before the infra or frontend subagent started
in the run log, each decision file was written by its subagent's session, not by the lead's
each decision file present has the level 2 headings Decision, Options considered, Rationale, Curated entries used, Catalog gaps, Assumptions
every id under Curated entries used in each decision file is an entries id in that specialist's catalog.json
Does the spec include a criterion or plan step that covers existing task rows getting a priority value when the column is added?
Do the spec's Design choices summarize and point to each decision file rather than contradict or ignore it?

cases.purpose: A conflict that changes acceptance criteria goes to the owner. The lead must not pick a side in the criteria.
cases.pilot: The pilot has sign-up and server-side sessions, and a committed decision file docs/decisions/auth.md that states: no session may be created before the user's email address is verified.

inline.title: Drop users straight into the dashboard after sign-up
inline.body: Sign-up has too much friction. After submitting the sign-up form the user should land in the dashboard immediately, signed in, with no email step in between.

tierReasons.evidence: Session creation moves earlier in the sign-up flow.

security.reason: Changes when a session is created.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json
status == "needs-owner"
escalations contains an item with kind == "ac-conflict" and at least 2 options
conflicts contains an item with changesAcceptanceCriteria == true whose between includes a path under docs/decisions/
the Open questions section of spec.md contains a line starting with "- [blocking]"
at least one acceptanceCriteria item has pendingEscalation == true
Does the spec avoid committing, in its acceptance criteria, to either creating a session before verification or requiring verification first?
Does each escalation option say what it would do to the acceptance criteria, so the owner can answer in one line?
